headline: The orchestrator's framing was the actual finding: three rounds running, a fix was correct about its own defect and created a new one in the same mechanism. Round 3 does not patch a third symptom — it writes ADR-032, which settles what a match set IS when a tier has two matchers, and then makes the code obey it.

wall_clock.constraint: Both suites reached their rounding step this round. `invariant` hit 17.22s against a 17.39s cliff (where the rule stops deriving 20) and `fast` recorded 91.04s against 91.30s.
wall_clock.answer: Removed waste rather than asking for a ceiling, which is ADR-021's own ruling quoted in ADR-029: the select step got its OWN budget (`SELECT_OPTIONS_WAIT_MS`, 1s) instead of borrowing `SETTLE_BUDGET_MS` (2s), and `LATE_OPTIONS_DELAY_S` went 0.5s -> 0.3s. Result: invariant 17.22 -> 15.82s, fast 91.04 -> 90.38s, with five cases added.
wall_clock.stated_honestly: The published band cites the ledger's slowest row at 229 (91.04s), and the margin quoted in ADR-019 section 2 is now 0.26s against that MAXIMUM rather than the larger number the published band implies — which is R13's lesson applied in the same commit that logs R13.

findings.semantics_settled: ADR-032 — a name tier resolves to exactly ONE match set per document. `scope_tiers` carries the exact locator and a folded alternative; `_resolve_in` counts the exact one ONCE and swaps in the folded one only if it is empty. Everything downstream (`near`, `index`, `many`, `n == 1`, M38's ambiguity bookkeeping) sees a single locator and cannot tell how it was chosen.
findings.which_option_and_why: Fallback, not union — the reviewer's first option, and the ADR says why the second is rejected: a union contains the case twins, so `index`, `near` and `many` read a set the plan was not written against, which is PR #60 R1 arriving by another route. Fallback also buys the stronger property the four falsified sentences were reaching for: if the page spells the name the plan's way, the fold is never consulted, at any tier, for any rule.
findings.red_first: resolver-index-selects-from-one-match-set (fast), `{'role':'link','name':'Add to cart','index':1}` on case-twins.html: on 04cc136 the run is `{'status':'success','answer':'Catalogue row CTA'}` — the SAME element `index: 0` returns. Expected `failure:locate`, which is what base 6b016b5 gave. Now `failure:locate`.

findings.cost: One extra `count()` per name tier per document. Every path except `near` was already paying it; `near` now pays it too, which is the price of proximity and indexing agreeing about what they select from.

findings.fix: The guard moved OUT of `_whole_string` and to the top of `resolve()`, before any locator is built, over `name`, `text`, `near` and `anchor`. `_whole_string` keeps a one-line check as a local invariant for a caller that does not route through `resolve`, and its docstring no longer claims to be the choke point — that claim is what R11 falsified.
findings.why_locate_not_task: `locate` is the class base 6b016b5 gave, and failure class is a graded output (INV-1). A `task`-class plan refusal is arguably more correct — it is a bad PLAN, not an absent element — but it means teaching `plan_gap` about value types, which was declined in round 1 for the same reason and is unchanged.
findings.suite_tags: All three `invariant`, not `fast`: they are must-always-hold diagnosis properties and the `fast` band could not pay for them. `resolver-non-string-target-is-a-locate-failure` (the `text` key) stays in `fast` as the representative.

findings.fix: New case `resolver-folded-name-with-a-slash-resolves` (fast) targeting a button on `case-twins.html` whose label is uppercased by stylesheet and contains `/` — so the exact pass finds nothing, the FOLDED pass runs, and it is the only pass that builds a regex. `button` stays in `resolve_advertised_except` on the inspector case (that exclusion is the ROLE disagreement T-M42-20-D4, a different thing), and this case reaches the crash directly instead.
findings.red_first: With `.replace("/", r"\\/")` deleted from resolver.py, the case is `failure:act`: `Error: Locator.count: InvalidSelectorError: Error while parsing selector `button[name=/^\\s*EXPORT\\s+AS\\s+\\.HTM\\s+/\\s+\\.HTML\\s+/\\s+\\.TXT\\s*$/i]` - unexpected symbol "\\" at position 40 during parsing attribute value`. With the escape in place it is `success`. The reviewer's own check — delete the escape, run the gate — now fails at this case instead of staying green.
findings.note: `trace_note_contains: narrowed: name-case-folded` is asserted too, so a case that stopped reaching the folded pass cannot pass for the wrong reason.
